key_insight: This paper introduces autoregressive Boltzmann Generators, aiming to improve equilibrium sampling for molecular systems by relaxing some of the expressivity limits of standard normalizing-flow-based BGs. The core idea is to keep the benefits of exact likelihoods and importance-sampling correction while enabling a more flexible generative model.
problem_solved: It addresses the difficulty of efficiently generating uncorrelated equilibrium samples from molecular systems, a key challenge in statistical physics and molecular simulation. Existing Boltzmann Generators built on normalizing flows can be too restrictive because of invertibility constraints that limit model expressivity.
method: Use an autoregressive generative architecture for Boltzmann Generators instead of relying only on traditional normalizing flows.
Preserve exact likelihood computation and combine it with importance sampling correction to sample equilibrium states efficiently.
Improve flexibility in representing complex molecular distributions while maintaining tractable training and sampling.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this work suggests a more expressive path for physics-aware generative modeling where strict flow constraints may no longer be necessary. It is especially relevant for scientific machine learning, molecular simulation, and any application requiring efficient sampling from complex high-dimensional distributions.
